title: Hawthorn berry decoction
subtitle: A traditional cardiac-supportive tonic
excerpt: One tablespoon of dried hawthorn berries simmered in 300 ml of cold water for 15-20 minutes, then strained. Traditionally taken as a long-term circulatory tonic. Important: do not use if you are on any cardiac medication without first consulting your prescriber.
sourceNotes: Maud Grieve, A Modern Herbal (1931), Hawthorn (Crataegus monogyna) entry. EMA HMPC Community herbal monograph on Crataegus spp. (2008, updated 2016) : cardiac tonic use and safety review. WHO Monograph on Crataegus spp. (Selected Medicinal Plants, Vol. 2, 2002).

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Dried berries store up to 12 months in a sealed tin away from light. Prepare each cup fresh.

glossaryTerms.definition: A preparation made by simmering harder plant material such as roots, berries, or bark in water to extract the active constituents. The liquid is strained and drunk.
A herb traditionally used to support the healthy function of the heart and circulation, not as a treatment for heart disease.

content.text: Hawthorn berry
decoction
is a simple hot preparation made by simmering one tablespoon of dried Crataegus monogyna berries in 300 ml of cold water for 15-20 minutes. Traditionally used in western European herbal practice as a
cardiac tonic

: a long-course preparation taken to support circulatory function in healthy adults. The berries are rich in flavonoids and oligomeric procyanidins. One cup twice daily, for courses up to three months. This herb has significant interactions with cardiac medication.

attrs.title: Precautions
attrs.body:
Not medical advice. Consult a qualified herbalist or doctor for ongoing or serious symptoms.

Hawthorn potentiates the action of digoxin, beta-blockers, and ACE inhibitors. Do not use this preparation if you take any cardiac medication without first consulting your prescriber. This herb is not suitable for readers with diagnosed heart conditions without their prescriber's guidance.

If you experience chest pain, breathlessness, palpitations, or dizziness at any time, stop the preparation and seek medical attention promptly.

Paediatric use is not adult-divided-by-half. Consult a herbalist who specialises in children's herbal medicine before using any herbal preparation in children under twelve.

content.text: Ingredients
Method
Place one tablespoon of dried hawthorn berries and 300 ml of cold water in a small saucepan. Starting from cold allows the active compounds to extract gradually.
Bring slowly to a gentle simmer over a low-medium flame. Cover the pan once simmering and cook for 15-20 minutes. The liquid should reduce slightly and turn a deep wine-red.
Remove from the heat. Strain through a fine sieve into a cup, pressing the berries lightly. Discard the spent herb.
Cool for five minutes and drink warm.
Dosing

One cup twice daily (morning and evening), prepared fresh each time. Hawthorn is a long-course tonic: take for up to three months, then take a four-week break before beginning another course. The tonic action builds over several weeks.
Storage
Dried berries store for up to 12 months in a sealed tin in a cool dark place. Prepare the
decoction
fresh each time; do not store the prepared liquid.
When not to use this remedy
Do not use this preparation if you have a heart condition or take cardiac medication (including digoxin. Beta-blockers, or ACE inhibitors) without your prescriber's guidance.
Stop and seek medical attention for chest pain, breathlessness, palpitations, or dizziness. These are not symptoms a home herbal preparation addresses.
